“World-Honored One!
"From where has this flower canopy come?
The Buddha said,
"O virtuous ones!"
As for these flower canopies, they were scattered and cast from afar by the great assembly of bodhisattvas from the world-system Adorned with All Joy, as an offering to this gathering.
Then this entire assembly addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

We wish to behold that world Adorned with All Joys and that World-Honored One, Tathāgata Subduer of Māras; we also wish to behold these hosts of Māras who have gone there, as well as the activities performed within their world.”
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the inclinations of the assembled multitude, addressed the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati, saying: "Good son!
This assembly now desires to see the world-system Sarvavyūhapratimaṇḍita, and they also wish to see that Tathāgata Mārajit."
"You should manifest this so that the entire great assembly may all behold it.

Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati, having received the Buddha’s instruction, immediately emitted ten thousand rays of light from between the ten toes of his feet. These lights shone universally throughout the eastern buddha-fields—equal in number to twelve *gaṅgā*-sands—and reached as far as the world-system called *Sarvasukhavyūha*, where they remained in continuous, vast, and brilliant radiance.
At that time, the entire great assembly in this gathering clearly beheld the world Adorned with All Pleasures, as well as the Tathāgata Subduer of Māras.
They also saw all the Māras within that Buddha’s assembly, seated upon the Dharma throne, extensively expounding the True Dharma of the Great Assembly for the sake of the multitude.

When the great assembly in this gathering saw these signs, they were struck with wonder. Each rose from their lotus seat and, facing the Tathāgata Subduer of Māra from afar, joined their palms in prostration and scattered exquisite flowers as an offering.
By the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha, World-Honored One, the scattered flowers formed a vast and magnificent pavilion of flowers above the crown of the Tathāgata Subduer of Māra.
At that time, the hosts of Māras addressed the Tathāgata Māradamanīya, saying:
"World-Honored One!
We now wish to return once more to the presence of Śākyamuni Buddha in the Sahā world."
That Buddha addressed them, saying:
"O sons of good family!
You may return; now is precisely the right time."

Thereupon, all those Māras prostrated themselves with their heads to the ground, paying homage at the feet of that Buddha, and circumambulated him seven times to the right. By the majestic spiritual power of the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati, they vanished from within that buddha-field and, after a mere moment, returned to this Sahā world. Having arrived, they prostrated themselves with their heads at the feet of Śākyamuni Buddha, circumambulated him seven times to the right, and withdrew to stand to one side, withdrawing their minds, focusing their attention, and reverently turning toward him.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the māras, saying:
"O worthy ones! Do you see that world called Sarvavyūhasukha?"
The Māras replied:
"We have indeed seen it,
O Venerable One!"
That land is rare, pure, and lovely; it is the supreme abode of purity and stainlessness.
Having seen it, we all resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Venerable Śāriputra said: "O noble ones!
Since you have already resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, you should no longer engage in the activities of Māra."
The Māra said: “No, Venerable One!”
If there are those who dwell securely in a profound and firm resolve, the assembly of bodhisattvas is then able to perform the activities of Māra. Why is this?
Because those bodhisattvas who dwell securely in a profound and firm resolve possess the power and capability to initiate demonic deeds as appropriate to each situation.
For this reason, Venerable One,
you should know that when any bodhisattva performs what appears to be the work of Māra, this is said to be the activity of a Buddha, not the activity of Māra.

At that time, after the various Māras had manifested their supernatural transformations within this Buddha-field, twenty thousand people among this assembly resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Furthermore, ten thousand sons of gods from the host of Māras also resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and with one voice and in unison, they spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!"
"We all vow to be reborn within that world adorned with all delights.
Having spoken these words, Śākyamuni Tathāgata then bestowed upon them this prophecy:
"You shall all be born within that buddha-field."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Regarding the Dharma of enlightenment of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas, many Māras and followers of external paths create obstacles and difficulties."

I only pray that the World-Honored One, by means of his majestic spiritual power, will establish this True Dharma so that it may long abide in the world, and further receive, protect, and sustain such profound sūtras as these.
World-Honored One!

If this sutra, by virtue of being sustained by the empowerment of the Buddha-Tathāgata, does not disappear but is instead upheld, recited, and widely disseminated, it will cause all hosts of Māras to find no opportunity to interfere.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati, saying: "Sāgaramati!
I now establish this True Dharma."

If there are sentient beings who wish to arouse diligence and bring various roots of goodness to maturity for the sake of transforming and delivering them, they should receive and uphold such profound sutras according to the Dharma and expound them for others.
Furthermore, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati, saying:
"Listen now attentively and apply your mind with great care!

That Dharma Master, having performed the recitation of these secret verses, shall purify his body and mind, bathe according to the ritual, don fresh and clean robes, and take his seat upon the lion throne;
facing the east, he shall scatter exquisite flowers and pray to the Buddhas, requesting their compassionate acceptance;

then, giving rise to great compassion for all sentient beings, he shall reverently contemplate that Śakra Devendra, out of pity, will come to arrange the assembly of those listening to the Dharma for him, ensuring they remain solemn and disciplined.

furthermore, wherever this True Dharma resides, I shall accept and sustain it, causing the Dharma to abide for a long time."

He thoroughly purifies his physical actions; he truthfully guards his verbal actions; he firmly stabilizes his mind and wisdom; he skillfully cultivates the practice of patience; he skillfully purifies the aggregate of ethical discipline; he skillfully exerts the power of diligence; he skillfully maintains the truths of extensive learning; he skillfully contemplates so as to harmonize and gladden the mind; he sharpens the faculty of wisdom to the utmost; he skillfully practices correct conduct; he skillfully protects the bodhicitta; he skillfully cultivates the contemplation of loving-kindness and establishes himself in great compassion, universally causing all sentient beings to ultimately be liberated from all suffering and affliction, and universally causing all sentient beings to obtain sublime bliss.

Once that Dharma-preacher has given rise to this thought, he should take his seat upon the lion throne and pray to the Great Brahmā King, requesting him to grant his compassionate acceptance; thereafter, he should preach the Dharma to others as appropriate.
Immediately, the Great Brahmā King, together with the assembly of Brahmās, came to where the Dharma teacher was to provide protection and support.

When the Great Brahmā King arrived at the time of the Dharma assembly, there were various auspicious signs: namely, that all those in the assembly gave rise to a mind of loving-kindness; or that the faculties of those in the assembly were complete and unimpaired;
or that they dwelt together in peace within the Dharma of Bodhi;
or that they took delight in the Dharma and the Dharma teacher, conceiving thoughts of reverence toward them.
Either they are free from all defilements;
or they focus the mind one-pointedly, remaining free from distraction;
or again, they bind their mindfulness to wholesome dharmas.
Either they collect their thoughts and cease all external hearing to listen to the Dharma with focused intent;
or, in the presence of a Dharma teacher, they are able to speak of various sublime Dharma-gates that have never been previously taught or heard before.
"If such signs as these appear, you should know that it is Mahābrahmā, King of the Brahmā Heaven, who has come to this Dharma assembly.
At that time, Mahābrahmā, being present in this assembly, rose from his seat, approached the Buddha, and said to him:
"World-Honored One!..."

"Wherever there may be anyone who proclaims such a profound and correct Dharma, I shall set aside all the immeasurable bliss of meditative concentration in my abode in the Brahma realm and immediately go to that place where the Dharma teacher resides to provide protection."
World-Honored One!
There are eight kinds of dharmas for bestowing protection.
What are these eight?
First, they provide protection for mindfulness, so that one does not forget the Dharma as it has been heard;
second, they provide protection for wisdom, so that one does not contradict the profound Dharma;
third, they provide protection for practice, so that one fully understands all meanings.
Fourth, he bestows protection upon eloquence, causing them to sever all doubts and delusions;
fifth, he bestows protection upon their prophetic declarations, causing all who hear their words and voices to rejoice;
sixth, he bestows protection upon the methods for transformation and deliverance, causing them to surpass and excel all assemblies.
Seventh, he bestows protection so that the light of the present life may be free from darkness and dullness;
eighth, he bestows protection so that one may attain the gateway of renunciation and practice according to the Dharma to achieve realization.
“World-Honored One!

By means of these eight dharmas, we shall skillfully provide protection for those Dharma-preachers; furthermore, we shall secretly and constantly guard them so that the Dharma may endure for a long time, and all demonic adversaries and disputes shall be entirely extinguished.
All of this is established through the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata, so that his True Dharma may spread widely.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We pray that the World-Honored One will, through his majestic spiritual power, establish this True Dharma so that it may endure for a long time.”

In the final age after the Tathāgata has entered parinirvāṇa, if there are sentient beings who have deeply planted roots of goodness, such that they may obtain this most profound sūtra, receive it into their hands, or place it in a casket to circulate it from one person to another so that it does not disappear.

At that time, having accepted the exhortation offered by Bodhisattva Sāgaramati, the World-Honored One emitted rays of light of various colors from between his eyebrows; these rays illuminated this trichiliocosm, pervading it with vast and brilliant radiance.
Within this trichiliocosm, all species of medicinal herbs, forest trees, sands, and stones, upon being touched by the light, were entirely transformed into the physical forms of the Tathāgata.
The manifested images all made offerings within the Great Jewel Adorned Bodhimanda.
Because they were established by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, the manifested images of the Tathāgatas immediately each spoke with one voice in unison, saying:
"World-Honored One, Śākyamuni Tathāgata!"
Because this True Dharma is established through majestic spiritual power, it is likewise established by the majestic spiritual power of all Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions.
Because it is established by the majestic spiritual power of those Buddhas, the various Māras are unable to create obstacles or difficulties for it.
World-Honored One!

Even if the hosts of Māra were as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and even if their power were increased and they exhausted all their courage and strength, they would ultimately be unable to raise difficulties against this True Dharma.

Why is this? Even if the great earth were to split and shatter, all the great oceans were to completely dry up, all the Mount Sumerus were to be crushed into fine dust, the wind could be bound, the sun and moon were to fall to the ground, forms and images were to appear in empty space, water were to be found within fire, and fire were to be found within water;

even if the four great elements were each to possess different natures, all sentient beings were to become one mind, and the two things of space and earth were to merge together—if such events as these were to occur, they still could not cause even the slightest dharma to move or shift within the sustaining power (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of the Buddha-Tathāgata.
At that time, the World-Honored One raised his right hand, placed it upon the crown of Venerable Ānanda’s head, and addressed him, saying: “Ānanda!

You should receive and uphold this True Dharma, and in the future final age, propagate and disseminate it widely, enabling others to receive, uphold, read, recite, and expound it, so that the Buddha’s True Dharma may long abide in the world.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
For what purpose do you entrust such a profound and sublime Dharma to the Bhikṣu Ānanda?”
Ānanda possesses knowledge that is limited;
however, there are great bodhisattvas in this assembly whose mindfulness and wisdom are as deep and vast as the great ocean, such that their depths cannot be known.
“Are these bodhisattvas not entrusted [with the teachings]?
The Buddha said,
“Sāgaramati!...”
It is not by his own power of wisdom that Ānanda is able to receive and uphold such True Dharma; it is entirely through the establishment of the Tathāgata’s majestic spiritual power.
You should now know this!

In the future final age, there will be sentient beings who, from Ānanda, hear and receive such profound and true Dharma; having heard it, they will believe and rejoice, giving rise to great joy and a sense of wonder, and should speak these words:
"All this is established by the inconceivable majestic power and spiritual authority of the Tathāgata, that a śrāvaka is able to thus uphold such profound and vast sūtras."
"This is due to the power of the Tathāgata’s majestic spiritual sustenance (*adhiṣṭhāna*).
At that time, among the assembly, there were some devas and humans who thought to themselves:
"Could there be any lapse in the power of the dhāraṇī-retention of that Bodhisattva Sāgaramati?"
"For what reason, Blessed One, do you say that Ānanda alone is foremost in learning?
At that time, the Venerable Mahākāśyapa, perceiving that the assembly harbored doubts, surveyed the great gathering and stepped forward to address the Buddha, saying:
"Blessed One!"
“Sāgaramati, how could there be any interval in the power of your mindfulness and dhāraṇī?
For what reason, World-Honored One, do you say only that Ānanda is foremost in much learning?
The Buddha said:
“Kāśyapa! Suppose that as many sentient beings as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River were gathered together and completely filled all the Buddha-fields.
What do you think?”
“Would that realm of sentient beings be considered many?
Kāśyapa replied to the Buddha,
“It would be very many, World-Honored One!”
"Very much so, Sugata!
The Buddha said, "Kāśyapa!"

Even if all such sentient beings were to simultaneously obtain human bodies, without one preceding or another following, and each were endowed with the power of mindfulness and dhāraṇī, being no different from the Venerable Ānanda;

If one were to compare the power of the dhāraṇī-recollection of all such sentient beings as mentioned above with the power of the dhāraṇī-recollection of the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati, it would not equal even a hundredth part; indeed, it would not equal even an *upaniṣad* part.
Kāśyapa!

This Bodhisattva Sāgaramati is able to uphold all the teachings spoken by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions without any obstruction; it is not that he is without obstruction regarding the teachings spoken by only one or two Buddhas.

For example, when rain falls into the great ocean, it is not that it can only accommodate one or two drops without obstruction; rather, it can accommodate all raindrops without any obstruction, yet that great ocean neither increases nor decreases.

Sāgaramati Bodhisattva is likewise; he is able to uphold all the teachings spoken by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, without any obstruction. It is not that he is without obstruction regarding the teachings spoken by only one or two Buddhas; rather, through the power of his mindfulness and dhāraṇī, there is neither increase nor decrease.
When this Dharma was being taught, eight thousand beings in the assembly gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and all spoke these words:
"We shall each vow to attain the power of the dhāraṇī of mindfulness, just like the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati."
At that time, the devas and humans in the assembly each took exquisite flowers and scattered them as an offering toward the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati.
Then, within that assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Padmavyūha who came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, having heard this profound Dharma-gate, believes and understands it, receives, maintains, reads, and recites it, examines it according to principle, and practices in accordance with the Dharma—how much merit will such a person obtain?”
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses in response to the Bodhisattva Padmavyūha:
"Even if one were to fill the entire trichiliocosm with pure gold and offer it to the Buddhas;
when one hears this treasury of Dharma and believes and understands it, this merit shall be far superior to the former."
Even if one were to fill ten thousand worlds with precious jewels and offer them to the Tathāgata,
if one can uphold and recite this profound sutra, the merit thereof would be incalculable compared to the former.
Furthermore, even if one were to fill ten thousand worlds with precious jewels and practice extensive giving,
if one can proclaim this profound sūtra, that merit would surpass the former beyond measure.
Even if one were to fill a thousand koṭis of buddha-fields with vast accumulations of precious jewels and offer them all to the Buddhas,
the World-Honored Ones, practicing this Dharma would be superior to that.
If one were to offer Buddha-fields adorned with jewels, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions, to the Tathāgatas;
yet when this Dharma is truly practiced and studied, its merit would be incalculable compared to the former.
These four dharmas possess boundless merit; even the Buddha could not describe their limit:
Generating the bodhicitta and protecting the Dharma, Giving rise to great compassion and practicing the path of Dharma.
These four dharmas possess immeasurable merit; when the wise hear them, they do not give rise to doubt:
the realm of space, the realm of sentient beings, the bodhicitta, and the wisdom of all Buddhas.
As I proclaim this precious Dharma, it causes billions of lands throughout the ten directions to tremble;
pure light is emitted and flowers rain down, while hundreds of kinds of music resound spontaneously without being struck.
All the Bodhisattvas, great sages of wisdom, Having aroused the most supreme resolve, offer this verse of praise;
Hearing this sublime Dharma-gate thus expounded, Each shall obtain excellent benefit, with no fruit in vain.
Having heard such a Dharma from me, sentient beings universally obtain all manner of wholesome benefits;
all this is due to the Tathāgata’s protection and sustenance, which causes them never to forget the bodhicitta.
Thousands of kotis of Buddhas from the ten directions, each with palms joined, prostrate in homage;
they praise the Great Holy Honored One, an ocean of virtues, who dwells well in empowerment, the Lion of the Śākyas.
Devas, nāgas, asuras, and kiṃnaras, Gandharvas, yakṣas, and the rest;
Brahmā, Śakra, and the world-protecting devas, Each standing in the air, spoke these words:
"May the Lion of the Śākyas long remain in the world, And may the supreme True Dharma never decline or vanish."
"O valiant Bodhisattvas, honored among the holy assembly, protect and uphold such profound and wondrous Dharma.
To those who receive and uphold this Eye of the Dharma, we shall go and manifest our forms;
honoring them and encouraging their diligence, we shall secretly guard them so that they suffer no decline or affliction."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati, saying: “Sāgaramati!

This present True Dharma is the Great Eye of the Dharma, the Seal of the Sublime Dharma, and the Banner of the Supreme Dharma; it definitively discerns all phenomena and analytically distinguishes all phenomena.”
Furthermore, those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present, all proclaim this Dharma.
Samudrareṇu!
As I have previously stated, you should honor and revere it, and with sincere resolve and firm steadfastness, practice in accordance with the principle.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the assembly of great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, headed by Sāgaramati, as well as all those in the world—devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others—hearing what the Buddha had taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.

In the eighteenth fascicle of the *Buddhabhāṣita-sāgaramati-paripṛcchā-vimala-mudrā-dharmaparyāya-sūtra*, Chengjuyi (澄舉意) intended to carve it into the Tripitaka. Zhao Shuichen (趙水臣), who had successively received several fascicles of this local compilation, read them and knew in his heart that they were not the words of the Buddha; he was unwilling to have them carved and returned them to Shuichen.
Later, upon obtaining the *Śrī-vaipulya-mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-sūtra* (The Sūtra of the Pure Seal), I found that every word and every phrase was nothing other than profound and wondrous meaning.
Believing this to be what was proclaimed from the golden mouth of the World-Honored One, my heart leaped with joy.
Several decades ago, I once dreamed that great waters filled the world, yet the people and the lands suffered no harm or obstruction;
I wandered and roamed within them with the same peace and joy as usual.
Upon awakening, he marveled at this, thinking: "This is beyond the reach of the human mind; could it not be a portentous omen?
Now, that this scripture begins with the title 'Auspicious Response' (Ruiying) perfectly accords with my dream;
thus, the manifestation of the dream in the past and the encounter with this scripture in the present seem no mere coincidence."

I, Cheng, pray that by means of these causes and conditions, my late father, the Grand Secretary Wenjing Gong Yan Ne, and my late mother, the First-Rank Lady Wu, may immediately be reborn in the Lotus Realm, where they shall behold the Buddha, hear the Dharma, and attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

Next, I shall deliver all enemies and kin, and all sentient beings, so that they may all attain the Buddha-way; if there were even a single sentient being who could not be delivered, I would not seek my own deliverance.
A letter from Shoudao Che Yancheng.
